title: An observation on Feynman diagrams with axial anomalous subgraphs in dimensional regularization with an anticommuting gamma5
claim: Reformulates Kreimer's anticommuting-gamma5 scheme with standard cyclic traces and a constructively defined gamma5-hat = -(i/4!) epsilon gamma gamma gamma gamma inserted at the boundary of the maximal 1PI non-singlet-type subgraph, averaging the two insertion points (eq. (1)) and, for closed chains with an odd number >= 3 of gamma5 vertices, over the vertices (eq. (3)). Computing the singlet axial current between the vacuum and two gluons shows that an extra counterterm proportional to the Chern-Simons current K^mu is needed from O(alpha_s^2) (Z_JK = -(1/2) n_f C_F alpha_s^2, eq. (22); gauge dependent at O(alpha_s^3)), so the bare ABJ equation does not hold automatically and the scheme does not give a constructive Adler-Bardeen proof.
loop_order: matrix elements to O(alpha_s^3) (VVA-type, 3-4 loops); AWI checks with massive quarks to O(alpha_s^2)
theory: QCD with singlet axial current; appendix: anomaly-free chiral (electroweak) theory
scheme: DREG, anticommuting gamma5 except gamma5-hat at prescribed positions (Kreimer-scheme variant), cyclic Dirac traces, pairs of epsilon tensors contracted with D-dimensional metrics (eq. (4))
symmetry_argument: axial Ward identity and ABJ equation tested explicitly; App. A proposes rules for (A.1) identifying external momenta of a fermion loop inside a diagram (averaging over external momenta, eqs. (30)-(31)) and (A.2) fixing the contraction order of multiple epsilon tensors: gamma5^2 = 1 on the same chain, no 4d Fierz/Chisholm identities, a fixed order for projector epsilons, symmetric average over pairings for epsilons from independent gamma5-odd loops (eq. (32)), D-dim metrics

proved: explicit computation: mismatch alpha_s^2 (4 n_f C_F) in the renormalized ABJ equation without the K^mu counterterm (eq. (20)); counterterm (eqs. (21)-(22))
AWI with massive quarks verified to O(alpha_s^2) with the revised renormalization
assumed: App. A rules for the full SM are stated as a conjecture to three-loop order, pending explicit calculations (authors' words: 'we believe' for A.1)
non-anomalous amplitudes need no extra renormalization (checked on examples only)
checked_partially: statement in the Introduction that reading prescription 'C' of Bednyakov-Pikelner (S5.11) reproduces the 4-loop SM strong-coupling beta function confirmed by S5.17 and S5.19, and is compatible with Kreimer's scheme

evidence: Sec. 2 (eqs. (1)-(4)); Sec. 3.2-3.3 (eqs. (6)-(9), (20)-(22)); Sec. 3.4; Conclusion; App. A.1-A.2 (eqs. (30)-(32)); remark that SM 1PI amplitudes with two gamma5-odd loops start at three loops and are UV finite as a whole
red_flags: different reading prescriptions agree at leading poles but can differ at epsilon^0 or in high-order poles (Introduction) - the precise statement of the reading-point ambiguity
epsilon-tensor products contracted in D dims: contraction order matters without the 4d Schouten identity; resolved only by a prescription (App. A.2)
the K^mu counterterm is not BRST-exact (author's remark): tension with gauge invariance for the operator renormalization
cross_checks: contradicts the automatic Adler-Bardeen expectation of S5.02_Kreimer1994 at O(alpha_s^2)
consistent with Larin-scheme results (S5.04, S5.05) once the extra counterterm is added (leading pole of Z_KJ matches Larin scheme, footnote 12)
notes: Most explicit modern statement of what the 'reading point' freedom does at 3-4 loops and what is still conjectural for the full SM.
